question: The angles of depression of two houses of the same height from the top of a building are 45° and 30° towards the east. If the two houses are 50 m apart, what will be the height of the building in metres?
solution:
**Given:**

The angle of depression of two houses of the same height from the building are 45° and 30° towards the east

Two houses are 50m apart

**Formula Used:**

tantheta=(height)/(Base)

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8a063089b7f5a24d6266e687f7052d89951702b2db6cbd1cb2be2de5d82c910b.png] 

⇒ Let the height of the building = h metre

⇒ and, BC = x metre

⇒ In bigtriangleupABC

⇒ tan45º = (AB)/(BC)

⇒ tan45º = (h)/(x)

⇒ 1 = (h)/(x)

⇒ h = x metre

⇒ In bigtriangleupADB

⇒ tan30º = (AB)/(BD)=(h)/(50+h)

⇒ (1)/(sqrt3)=(h)/(50+h)

⇒ 50 + h = sqrt3h

⇒ (sqrt3-1)h = 50

⇒ h=(50)/(sqrt3-1)=(50)/(sqrt3-1)times(sqrt3+1)/(sqrt3+1)=(50(sqrt3+1))/((sqrt3)²-1²)=(50(sqrt3+1))/(3-1)=(50(sqrt3+1))/(2)=25(sqrt3+1)

⇒ **Hence, The height of the building is 25(sqrt3+1)** **m**
